581892.title: The Clear shifts question ignores lines not approved or declined (release)
581892.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit and Schedule access, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example Esther Howard) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Technician {Technician-B} (for example Ralph Edwards) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on, the Service department, and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST S4R28 Approved Lines") is used by this case only.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S10043-17641) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has an approved line {Line-1} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and a line that is not approved, {Line-2} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch"), saved with Line Approved off.
  • Work order {Work-order-2} (for example S10043-17642) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has an approved line {Line-3} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and a declined line {Line-4} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch").
  • Work order {Work-order-3} (for example S10043-17643) for {Customer-A} is led by {Technician-A} and has two approved lines, {Line-5} (for example "Service - Full grease service") and {Line-6} (for example "Service - Adjust clutch").
  • {Technician-A} has a shift tomorrow 8:00–10:00 on {Work-order-1} that covers {Line-1} and not {Line-2}.
  • {Technician-A} has a shift tomorrow 10:00–12:00 on {Work-order-2} that covers {Line-3} and not {Line-4}.
  • {Technician-A} has a shift tomorrow 13:00–15:00 on {Work-order-3} made with Choose lines, with both {Line-5} and {Line-6} ticked.
  • No other shift is booked on {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2} or {Work-order-3}.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
581892.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and click Board View in the display switcher.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Drag {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
  4. Read the title of the question that opens.
  5. Click Keep shifts.
  6. Drag {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
  7. Read the title of the question that opens.
  8. Click Keep shifts.
  9. Drag {Work-order-3} from {Technician-A}'s column into {Technician-B}'s column.
  10. Read the title of the question that opens.
  11. Click Keep shifts.
  12. Click Schedule in the top menu.
  13. Use the arrow next to Today to go to tomorrow.
  14. Read {Technician-A}'s shifts on {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3}.
581892.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the All tab opens in Board View, with a column for each technician.
  • Step 2: only {Customer-A}'s work orders show: {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3}, in {Technician-A}'s column.
  • Step 3: a question opens.
  • Step 4: the question is titled "Clear {Technician-A}'s scheduled shifts?" (with the example name: "Clear Esther Howard's scheduled shifts?"). The line that is not approved ({Line-2}) is ignored.
  • Step 5: after Keep shifts {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-B}'s column.
  • Step 6: a question opens.
  • Step 7: the question is titled "Clear {Technician-A}'s scheduled shifts?" (with the example name: "Clear Esther Howard's scheduled shifts?"). The declined line ({Line-4}) is ignored.
  • Step 8: after Keep shifts {Work-order-2} moves to {Technician-B}'s column.
  • Step 9: a question opens.
  • Step 10: the question is titled "Clear {Technician-A}'s scheduled shifts?" (with the example name: "Clear Esther Howard's scheduled shifts?"). A Choose lines shift that ticks every approved line counts.
  • Step 11: after Keep shifts {Work-order-3} moves to {Technician-B}'s column.
  • Step 12: the Schedule opens.
  • Step 13: the Schedule shows tomorrow's date.
  • Step 14: all three of {Technician-A}'s shifts are still on the Schedule tomorrow, at the same times.

Release copy of C581892 (in the Fast-follow folder). It leaves out the message shown after each lead change, which waits on SV-11522 / SV-11524: Chris Ward (product owner) made these fast-follows for after the release (Slack, 20 Oct 2026, https://shopview.slack.com/archives/C0C41RV3T3L/p1792455057423139).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-R28 (reworded in version 49 from Chris Ward's answer 1 of 14 Oct 2026 to our question sheet: only approved lines count, judged when the lead changes), S4-R29 and S4-R23, read 19 Oct 2026. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R28: “The shift-clearing prompt (S4-R11, S4-R26) shows only when the outgoing lead has a work-order-level shift on this work order that has not ended. A work-order-level shift is one that covers every approved line of the work order, judged at the moment the lead changes; this is what the Schedule's Entire work order drop creates. Lines not yet approved, and declined lines, are ignored. On a work order with one line, a shift on that line counts, and so does a Choose lines shift that ticks every approved line. A shift on only some approved lines does not show the prompt, and that includes an Entire work order shift once a line has been added and approved after it was made.”
  • S4-R29: “The prompt reads: title “Clear {Name}'s scheduled shifts?” (with no name: “Clear the lead technician's scheduled shifts?”); text “{Name} has shifts scheduled for this whole work order. Clearing removes shifts that haven't started and ends one that's under way now. Shifts on individual lines and recorded time don't change.”; buttons “Keep shifts”, “Clear shifts” and “Cancel”.”
  • S4-R23: “If the user chooses to keep shifts, change the lead technician and retain the existing shifts.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

AUTOMATION: READY
why: Left out: the message after each lead change ("... assigned to ...", with Undo), from the results of steps 5, 8 and 11.
Removed the S4-R5 quote and its mention in the Source paragraph (it backed only the message).
Removed the Known problem paragraph (SV-11524).

The grouped results "Steps 4, 7 and 10" and "Steps 5, 8 and 11" are split into one "Step N:" result per step; results added for the steps that had none (1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 12, 13), saying only what the screen shows.
Steps and preconditions unchanged (14 steps). AUTOMATION changed to READY.

97002.title: Dragging a card changes its lead, dragging to Unassigned clears it (release)
97002.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 20 minutes
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043). Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher).
  • Role: Owner/Admin. On a QA branch sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders). This user is the dispatcher.
  • Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  • Technicians (examples, the expected results call them by first name or full name): "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo", "ZZAUTOTEST Cal Charlie". A staff member counts as a technician when, in Settings > Staff > the staff member's edit icon > Edit Staff Member, they are Active, Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customers (used by this case only, each with one contact and one asset): "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change Golf Co". The steps and expected results call them by the end of the name ("Alpha Co", "Golf Co").
  • Work orders (all Approved): lead Ana — Alpha Co; no lead — Golf Co.
  • None of these technicians has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders (check the Schedule page). If a window titled "Clear … scheduled shifts?" still appears during a move, click "Keep shifts".

Setup

  1. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: confirm "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo", "ZZAUTOTEST Cal Charlie" exist and count as technicians at this location (edit icon > Edit Staff Member). To add one: New Staff Member with those settings (at least one Department is required) (e.g. first name "ZZAUTOTEST Ana", last name "Alpha") > Save & Close.
  2. Create this case's customers: "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change Golf Co". For each: top menu Customers > New Customer, Name > Save; on the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact); then the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  3. Create each work order listed in the Preconditions: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. Move it to the status named: a new work order starts as Estimate (it opens with the New Line form: pick a ready-made line and Save & Close); for Approved turn on Line Approved on its line; for In Progress click Start on the line's Labor row (stop the clock afterwards with Stop > Clock Out); for Review click the line's Complete button, type a Tech Story (fill any missing detail it asks for, e.g. Mileage) and click Complete Line (the List shows "Ready For Review"); for Complete then click Mark Reviewed, enter the VIN if asked and click Confirm Review; for Declined save the line with Line Approved off and click Decline on it (it must be the work order's only line); for Invoiced complete and review it first, then Finance tab > Create Invoice; for Paid, after invoicing, Finance tab > New Payment for the full amount > Make Payment. Set the lead technician before invoicing. Once the work order is Approved, pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page (leave it as Unassigned for an unassigned one). (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Write down each work order number as you create it (e.g. S1-801); the steps call each work order by the end of its customer name (e.g. "Alpha Co").
  4. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > List > type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change" in Search — exactly 2 work orders show, both Approved: Alpha Co led by Ana, Golf Co with no lead (Unassigned). On the Schedule neither has a shift. If anything differs, correct that work order (status or Lead Technician) before starting.
97002.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Drag Lead Change" in Search so only this case's work orders show.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher (tooltip "Board View").
  4. Drag the Alpha Co card from Ana's column into Ben's column and release.
  5. Click the Alpha Co card to open the work order and read its Lead Technician, then go back with the browser Back button.
  6. Drag the Alpha Co card from Ben's column into the Unassigned column and release.
  7. Open the Alpha Co work order again, read Lead Technician, then go back.
  8. Drag the Golf Co card from the Unassigned column into Cal's column and release.
  9. Open the Golf Co work order, read Lead Technician, then go back.
  10. Click Tech View in the display switcher at the right of the toolbar (tooltip "Tech View").
  11. Drag the Golf Co row from Cal's group into Ana's group and release, then open it and read Lead Technician.
97002.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the Work Orders page shows the All tab.
  • Step 2: only this case's work orders show (Alpha Co and Golf Co).
  • Step 3: Board View shows a column for each technician and an Unassigned column. Alpha Co is in Ana's column and Golf Co is in the Unassigned column.
  • Step 4: the card sits in Ben's column.
  • Step 5: the work order page shows Lead Technician Ben Bravo.
  • Step 6: the card sits in Unassigned.
  • Step 7: the work order page shows no lead technician.
  • Step 8: the Golf Co card moved into Cal's column.
  • Step 9: the Golf Co work order page shows Lead Technician Cal Charlie.
  • Step 10: Tech View shows a group for each technician, with the Golf Co row in Cal's group.
  • Step 11: in Tech View the row moves to Ana's group and the work order page shows Lead Technician Ana Alpha.

Release copy of C97002 (in the Fast-follow folder). It leaves out the message shown after each lead change and how long it stays open, which waits on SV-11522 / SV-11524: Chris Ward (product owner) made these fast-follows for after the release (Slack, 20 Oct 2026, https://shopview.slack.com/archives/C0C41RV3T3L/p1792455057423139).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns); SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S9-R6, S9-R7, read 19 Oct 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R6: “Between-technician moves reassign the lead under Story 4.”
  • S9-R7: “Moving a work order to Unassigned removes its lead; moving it out assigns the destination lead.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

AUTOMATION: READY
why: Left out: the message after the drags of steps 4 and 6 ("... assigned to ...", "... moved to Unassigned", Undo) and its close time (about 5 seconds).
Removed the S4-R5 and S4-R16 quotes and their mention in the Source paragraph; removed the Known problem paragraph (SV-11524).
The grouped result "Steps 8 and 9" is split into Step 8 and Step 9; results added for steps 1, 2, 3 and 10.

Steps and preconditions unchanged (11 steps). The Setup block still mentions the Reassign lead technician dialog, but only as the way to give an Estimate its lead; this case has no Estimate, so no step uses it.
AUTOMATION changed to READY.

97007.title: A lead set on the work order page sends it to the bottom (release)
97007.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • User {User-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dispatcher Two) has Work orders > View and Create & Edit at {Location-A} and is signed in in a second browser.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha), {Technician-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo) and {Technician-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Cal Charlie) are active staff members at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customers {Customer-A} to {Customer-E} are used by this case only, their names start with the same words (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Reassign Bottom") and end, in name order, with Aardvark Co, Abbey Co, Bravo Co, Delta Co and Echo Co.
  • Approved work orders: {Work-order-3} (for {Customer-C}) and {Work-order-4} (for {Customer-D}) are led by {Technician-B}; {Work-order-1} (for {Customer-A}), {Work-order-2} (for {Customer-B}) and {Work-order-5} (for {Customer-E}) are led by {Technician-C} (for example S10043-17721 to S10043-17725).
  • Nobody has reordered {Technician-B}'s work at {Location-A}, so {Technician-B}'s column starts in customer-name order: {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-4}.
  • No technician has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
97007.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type the shared start of the customer names (for example ZZAUTOTEST F3 Reassign Bottom) in Search.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  4. Open {Work-order-2}, pick {Technician-B} in Lead Technician on the work order page, then go back to Work Orders > All > Board View with the same search.
  5. Read the order of {Technician-B}'s column.
  6. Drag {Work-order-5}'s card from {Technician-C}'s column and drop it between {Work-order-3} and {Work-order-4} in {Technician-B}'s column.
  7. Click Tech View in the display switcher and read {Technician-B}'s group.
  8. In the second browser, as {User-B}, open Work Orders > All, type the same search, and read {Technician-B}'s work in Tech View and in Board View.
97007.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the Work Orders page shows the All tab.
  • Step 2: only this case's work orders show.
  • Step 3: Board View shows {Technician-B}'s column reading {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-4}. {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-5} are in {Technician-C}'s column.
  • Step 4: {Work-order-2}'s work order page shows Lead Technician {Technician-B}, and Board View shows again with the same search.
  • Step 5: {Technician-B}'s column reads {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-4}, {Work-order-2}. A lead set on the work order page goes to the bottom, even though by customer name it would come first.
  • Step 6: {Work-order-5} lands where it was dropped. {Technician-B}'s column reads {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-5}, {Work-order-4}, {Work-order-2}.
  • Step 7: Tech View shows the same order in {Technician-B}'s group.
  • Step 8: {User-B} sees the same order in both views.

Release copy of C97007 (in the Fast-follow folder). It leaves out giving a new lead from the lead technician dialog in the card's More actions menu, which waits on SV-11522 / SV-11524: Chris Ward (product owner) made these fast-follows for after the release (Slack, 20 Oct 2026, https://shopview.slack.com/archives/C0C41RV3T3L/p1792455057423139).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns); SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S9-R14 and S2-R6, read 19 Oct 2026. In version 53 (15 Oct 2026) S2-R6 was reworded to spell out the List's tie-break and to point to S9-R14; the expected results are unchanged. Starting order (customer name A to Z): Review Decisions page 853901313, DR-45 (29 Sep 2026). Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R14: “A work order that gets a new lead from the lead technician dialog (Assign or Reassign lead technician) or from its detail page goes to the bottom of the new technician’s work, for everyone at the location, in both views. A work order dragged to a technician goes where it is dropped. Removing the lead with the menu’s Unassign action (S11-R9) or on the detail page puts the work order in Unassigned in the initial sort, not at the bottom, so it is not lost behind every other unassigned work order. Going to the bottom applies only to work moved onto a technician. A work order created or split off with a lead keeps the initial sort (S9-R3).”
  • S2-R6: “Before a manual order is saved, use the List’s default work order sort, ties included, exactly as the List sorts today: work orders for the same customer go by start date, newest first. The List itself does not change. A work order that gets a new lead after it was created goes to the bottom of that technician’s work instead (S9-R14).”

AUTOMATION: READY

The orders in the later results no longer include {Work-order-1}: step 5 now reads {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-4}, {Work-order-2} and step 6 reads {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-5}, {Work-order-4}, {Work-order-2}.

97008.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Customer {Customer-A} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Invoiced Lock") is used by this case only and has six work orders (for example S10043-17811 to S10043-17816): {Work-order-1} Approved, {Work-order-2} Invoiced, {Work-order-3} Paid, {Work-order-4} Declined and {Work-order-5} Complete, all led by {Technician-A}, and {Work-order-6} Invoiced with no lead technician.

  • No technician has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders.

97009.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type the name of {Customer-A} in Search.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  4. Look at the {Work-order-2} and {Work-order-3} cards and hover the lock or any marker on them.
  5. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card above {Work-order-1}'s card inside {Technician-A}'s column and release it.
  6. Drag {Work-order-2}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column and release it.
  7. Drag {Work-order-3}'s card into the Unassigned column and release it.
  8. Drag {Work-order-6}'s card from Unassigned into {Technician-A}'s column and release it.
  9. Drag {Work-order-4}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column and release it, then drag {Work-order-5}'s card into {Technician-B}'s column and release it.
  10. Click Tech View in the display switcher.
  11. Drag {Work-order-3}'s row into {Technician-B}'s group and release it.

  • Step 1: the Work Orders page shows the All tab.
  • Step 2: only {Customer-A}'s work orders show.
  • Step 3: Board View shows {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-4} and {Work-order-5} in {Technician-A}'s column and {Work-order-6} in the Unassigned column.

  • Step 7: {Work-order-3} cannot be dropped on Unassigned. It stays in {Technician-A}'s column, no lead-change message appears and {Technician-A}'s count is unchanged.
  • Step 8: {Work-order-6} cannot be moved out of Unassigned. It stays there.
  • Step 9: {Work-order-4} (Declined) and {Work-order-5} (Complete) move to {Technician-B}'s column.
  • Step 10: Tech View shows {Work-order-3}'s row in {Technician-A}'s group.
  • Step 11: the same rule holds in Tech View. While {Work-order-3}'s row is over {Technician-B}'s group, the note "Paid · can’t be reassigned" shows at the top of that group, and {Work-order-3} stays in {Technician-A}'s group.

An Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned.
